nodes.title: SG-2.6 · Create the asset files that manifest.json references
nodes.body:
Context: game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room/manifest.json lists ten the-boys-room assets (backgrounds/bedroom-room.svg, furniture/bed.svg, bookshelf.svg, desk.svg, objects/old-computer.svg, window.svg, door.svg, characters/boy-sheet.svg, effects/dust.svg, audio/ambient-room.wav). Today only manifest.json lives under game/public; the files exist solely under game/frontend/public/assets. Desired behavior: the ten files exist under game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room. Expected result: every manifest path resolves to a real file. Why: the asset architecture keeps content under game/public/assets and the loader must not report missing assets.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given game/public/assets as the root, When each of the ten listed manifest paths is resolved, Then a non-empty file exists
- Given the manifest, When parseManifest runs, Then it still returns ok
- Given the files, When inspected, Then each SVG is well-formed and the WAV has a RIFF/WAVE header


## Scope
- In scope: Ten asset files under game/public/assets/worlds/the-boys-room
- Out of scope: Editing manifest.json
- Out of scope: ui/* assets
- Out of scope: Runtime or loader changes
- Out of scope: Final production artwork
- Preserve: manifest.json content
- Preserve: game/frontend/public/assets files
- Preserve: existing tests


## Technical constraints
- Temporary pixel-art SVGs with shape-rendering crispEdges
- Do not touch .ai-dlc or context.md


## Definition of done
- All ten files exist at the manifest paths
- New unit tests pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Manifest SVG image and spritesheet assets exist under game/public/assets
nodes.body:
Context: backgrounds/bedroom-room.svg, furniture/{bed,bookshelf,desk}.svg, objects/{old-computer,window,door}.svg, characters/boy-sheet.svg and effects/dust.svg are referenced by manifest.json but missing under game/public/assets. Desired behavior: each exists with width/height equal to the manifest dimensions. Why: pixel-art friendly assets must not be stretched.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the manifest, When each of the nine SVG paths is resolved under game/public/assets, Then a file exists
- Given each SVG, When its root width and height attributes are read, Then they equal the manifest dimensions
- Given each SVG, When parsed, Then it starts with an svg root element using crispEdges rendering


## Scope
- In scope: Nine SVG files
- Out of scope: Audio
- Out of scope: manifest edits
- Preserve: frontend/public copies


## Technical constraints
- Dimensions from manifest.json: 320x180, 100x35, 44x90, 70x28, 30x34, 60x50, 40x80, 64x48, 4x4


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- Nine SVGs present and dimension-correct


## Clarifying questions
- None

- SVG width/height equal manifest dimensions
- SVG root is svg with crispEdges

- Preserve: existing tests

nodes.summary: Unit tests for the nine SVG manifest paths
nodes.description: Add game/tests/publicAssetSvgs.test.ts. It reads the real manifest.json and the static asset files read-only (no writes, no app, no network) and asserts each SVG path exists with matching dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: SVG root is svg with crispEdges
technical_constraints: vitest; resolve root as ../public/assets via import.meta.url

steps.action: Load manifest.json via readFileSync, filter assets whose path ends with .svg and starts with worlds/ (nine entries). Add it('every svg path exists under public/assets') asserting the missing-list equals []; it('svg width and height match manifest dimensions') parsing width="N" height="N" with a regex and comparing to asset.dimensions; it('svg is crispEdges') asserting the content contains '<svg' and 'shape-rendering="crispEdges"'.
steps.command: cd game && npx vitest run tests/publicAssetSvgs.test.ts
